newsitem.title: CHINA: HK ELECTRIC H1 NET BOOSTED BY PROPERTY.
newsitem.headline: HK ELECTRIC H1 NET BOOSTED BY PROPERTY.

text.p: Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd reported a 21 percent rise in first-half net profit on Thursday, buoyed by property-related profits, while its core business grew by a steady 5.9 percent.
The company said net profit for the six months to June 30 rose to HK$2.09 billion fromHK$1.72 billion.
"The main increase in the profit resulted from the successful sales of car-parking spaces at Secan's South Horizons' development," Hongkong Electric said in a statement.
Secan Ltd is an associate of Hongkong Electric and is involved in the development of the South Horizons residential development in Ap Lei Chau in Hong Kong.

Hongkong Electric said poor weather had dampened demand growth during the first six months. But it expected encouraging demand growth in the future due to continuing completion of major buildings in Hong Kong's Central district and other areas.
"Our group is aggressively pursuing profitable investment opportunities outside Hong Kong, through its wholly-owned subsidiary, Hongkong Electric International Ltd (HEI)," the company added.

HEI signed a joint venture agreement in June with Siam Steel Pipe Group to construct and operate a 450 Megawatt gas fired power plant in the Rayong Industrial Park in Thailand. HEI has a 25 percent stake in the joint venture.
"This projects marks the group's entry into the international energy business, and other overseas projects are currently being studied," Hongkong Electric said.
